description: H-2 (High): the OAuth deep-link handoff has no Android receiver and no app-side handling. The backend OAuth callback (backend/src/routes/oauth.ts) mints a one-time app code and 302-redirects to config.appDeepLink (default threshold://auth/complete?code=...). For the native app to receive it, Android needs a VIEW/BROWSABLE intent-filter for the `threshold` scheme and app code that reads the incoming link and calls POST /oauth/exchange. Neither exists: app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml declares only the MAIN/LAUNCHER intent-filter, and app/lib/** has no deep-link handling. Also, README.md describes OAuth as 'built' when the native handoff is not end-to-end. Implement the concrete, CI-verifiable manifest fix, add app-side deep-link handling wired toward POST /oauth/exchange (ProductionAuthPort), and correct the README to stop overstating the auth flow. ENVIRONMENT NOTE: the Android SDK is NOT installed here, so `flutter build apk --release` cannot be run locally — the manifest change is validated by the CI android job (which asserts the merged release manifest). flutter analyze and flutter test MUST stay green locally.
steps: Add a deep-link receiver to app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml on the existing .MainActivity (which is android:exported=true, launchMode=singleTop). Add a SECOND <intent-filter> alongside the existing MAIN/LAUNCHER one: <intent-filter> <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/> <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT"/> <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE"/> <data android:scheme="threshold" android:host="auth"/> </intent-filter>. The scheme must match config.appDeepLink (threshold://auth/complete). Do NOT remove or alter the existing MAIN/LAUNCHER filter or any permission (RECORD_AUDIO/INTERNET must remain). Keep the comment style consistent with the file (reference FR-1.x / HIGH-18 / H-2 and no em/en dashes). Note: an App Links autoVerify over HTTPS is the more robust option the audit mentions, but the backend currently redirects to the custom scheme threshold://, so the custom-scheme VIEW/BROWSABLE filter is the correct minimal match to the server contract; document that an HTTPS App Link is a future hardening.

Add app-side deep-link handling that extracts code/error from the incoming threshold://auth/complete link and drives the backend exchange. Keep it analyze-clean and test-friendly WITHOUT adding a heavy native plugin that would require an Android build to verify (the sandbox cannot build the APK). Approach: define a small pure port, e.g. app/lib/session/auth_deep_link.dart with a parser `AuthDeepLink parse(Uri uri)` returning a sealed result {code: String} | {error: String} | invalid, plus an interface `AuthExchangeClient { Future<AuthResult> exchange(String code); }` that POSTs /oauth/exchange and verifies the returned session token. Wire ProductionAuthPort.reauthenticate() so that, instead of unconditionally throwing, it is structured to (a) trigger the OAuth start/redirect, (b) await the incoming deep link, (c) parse it, and (d) call AuthExchangeClient.exchange(code). The live link-listening and HTTPS client remain device/network bound, so where that runtime cannot run, ProductionAuthPort may still throw DeviceBindingUnavailable for the live link step, BUT the parser and the exchange-contract code must be real, pure, and unit-tested. The key behavioral fix is: the app now HAS deep-link parsing + exchange wiring, so the server half is no longer orphaned.

Add unit tests under app/test/session/ for the deep-link parser: parse threshold://auth/complete?code=abc123 -> code 'abc123'; parse threshold://auth/complete?error=access_denied -> error 'access_denied'; parse a link with neither code nor error -> invalid; parse a foreign scheme/host -> invalid. If an AuthExchangeClient with an injectable HTTP transport is added, test that a 200 {session, expiresAt} yields AuthResult.verified and a non-200 / missing session yields AuthResult.failed, using a fake transport (no real network). Keep all tests headless (no device).

Correct README.md to stop overstating OAuth as end-to-end complete. In the 'Status' section (around the line listing 'the backend request handling (OAuth with PKCE, webhook, ...)'), add an explicit, dash-free note that the backend OAuth-with-PKCE flow is implemented and tested, but the native Android deep-link handoff that delivers the one-time code to the app (threshold://auth/complete -> POST /oauth/exchange) and the live backend session client (ProductionAuthPort) are part of the deferred device adapters, so sign-in is not yet end-to-end on device. Keep wording consistent with the existing honest 'Status' tone. No em/en dashes.

Run `export PATH=/opt/flutter/bin:$PATH && cd app && flutter pub get && git checkout analysis_options.yaml pubspec.lock` (revert pub side effects unless pubspec intentionally changed), then `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` (must be clean), `flutter test` (all pass, incl new deep-link tests), and `dart run tool/lint_ui_copy.dart lib` (OK). If a new runtime dependency was unavoidably added to pubspec.yaml, keep pubspec.yaml and the resulting pubspec.lock change (do not revert those), and justify it; prefer NOT adding a native plugin so the analyze/test gates fully cover the change in this environment.

Author commits as the user (git -c user.name="Suleiman" -c user.email="85356587+suletetes@users.noreply.github.com" commit ...). Suggested atomic split: COMMIT 1 = AndroidManifest deep-link intent-filter; COMMIT 2 = app-side deep-link parser + exchange wiring + tests; COMMIT 3 = README Status correction. Stage only the relevant files per commit. Report explicitly that the Android release-APK build + permission assertion could NOT be run locally (no Android SDK) and is relied upon via the CI android job.
acceptance_criteria: AndroidManifest.xml declares a VIEW/BROWSABLE intent-filter for the `threshold` scheme (host auth) on .MainActivity, matching config.appDeepLink, with the existing MAIN/LAUNCHER filter and RECORD_AUDIO/INTERNET permissions intact.

The app has real, unit-tested deep-link parsing (code/error/invalid) and exchange-contract wiring toward POST /oauth/exchange, so the server-side one-time-code handoff is no longer orphaned on the client.
README.md Status no longer implies OAuth sign-in is end-to-end on device; it states the native deep-link handoff and ProductionAuthPort are deferred device adapters.
flutter analyze --fatal-infos is clean, flutter test passes (including the new deep-link tests), and the UI-copy dash lint passes.
Commits are atomic and user-authored; the inability to run the Android release-APK build locally is reported (relied on CI).
verification: export PATH=/opt/flutter/bin:$PATH && cd app && flutter pub get && git checkout analysis_options.yaml pubspec.lock || true; flutter analyze --fatal-infos && flutter test && dart run tool/lint_ui_copy.dart lib
findings:
H-2 remediated on branch fix/audit-findings-remediation in three atomic, user-authored commits (Suleiman).

COMMIT 1 (c0249b7) fix(app): register OAuth deep-link intent-filter for threshold scheme (H-2). Added a SECOND intent-filter to app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml on the existing .MainActivity (still exported=true, launchMode=singleTop): action VIEW + categories DEFAULT and BROWSABLE + data scheme=threshold host=auth, matching config.appDeepLink (default threshold://auth/complete, confirmed in backend/src/config.ts line 134 and used in backend/src/routes/oauth.ts). The existing MAIN/LAUNCHER filter and all permissions (RECORD_AUDIO, INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT) are untouched. A dash-free comment documents the FR-1.5/HIGH-18/H-2 rationale and notes an HTTPS App Link with autoVerify as future hardening (the backend currently redirects to the custom scheme, so the custom-scheme filter is the correct minimal match today).

COMMIT 2 (83172f6) fix(app): add OAuth deep-link parser and exchange wiring to ProductionAuthPort (H-2). New app/lib/session/auth_deep_link.dart: pure, total parseAuthDeepLink(Uri) returning a sealed AuthDeepLink { AuthDeepLinkCode | AuthDeepLinkError | AuthDeepLinkInvalid } (foreign scheme/host or missing code+error = invalid; non-empty code wins over error), plus the AuthExchangeClient contract and BackendAuthExchangeClient, which POSTs {code} to /oauth/exchange via an injectable AuthExchangeTransport and returns AuthResult.verified only on a 200 carrying a non-empty JSON `session` (per the oauth.ts {session, expiresAt} contract), else AuthResult.failed (non-200, non-JSON, missing session, empty code, or transport throw). app/lib/app/production_adapters.dart ProductionAuthPort now has a const constructor taking an optional AuthExchangeClient; reauthenticate() still throws DeviceBindingUnavailable for the device/network-bound live browser+link-listen step, but a new pure completeFromDeepLink(Uri, {client}) parses the already-received link and drives the exchange, so the server-side one-time-code handoff is no longer orphaned. providers.dart updated to const ProductionAuthPort() to satisfy prefer_const_constructors. Tests: new app/test/session/auth_deep_link_test.dart (18 tests) covering parser cases (code, error, neither, empty code, code-wins-over-error, foreign scheme, foreign host), the exchange contract via a fake transport (200+session verifies and posts the code to /oauth/exchange, non-200 fails, missing session fails, non-JSON fails, empty code fails without touching transport, transport failure fails), and completeFromDeepLink wiring (code redeems and verifies, error does not resume, invalid does not resume, no-client fails closed, live reauthenticate still deferred). No native plugin and no new pubspec dependency were added, so analyze and test fully cover the change; analysis_options.yaml and pubspec.lock pub side effects were reverted (no diff).

COMMIT 3 (018e4bf) docs: note OAuth sign-in is not yet end-to-end on device (H-2). README.md Status section now states the backend OAuth-with-PKCE flow is implemented and tested, but sign-in is not yet end-to-end on device: the native Android deep-link handoff (threshold://auth/complete to POST /oauth/exchange) and the live ProductionAuthPort session client are deferred device adapters, while the app ships the parser and exchange contract so the server-side handoff is wired. Dash-free, consistent with the existing honest Status tone.

VERIFICATION (local, Flutter 3.38.10 / Dart 3.10.9 pinned to CI): `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` prints 'No issues found!'; `flutter test` prints 'All tests passed!' at 678 tests (the 18 new deep-link tests are included, up from the prior baseline); `dart run tool/lint_ui_copy.dart lib` prints 'OK, no forbidden dashes in lib'. The acceptance grep for 'android.intent.action.VIEW' in the manifest matches (line 53).

ENVIRONMENT LIMITATION (explicit): the Android release-APK build (`flutter build apk --release`) and the CI android job's assertion that RECORD_AUDIO and INTERNET survive R8 in the merged release manifest COULD NOT be run locally because the Android SDK is NOT installed in this sandbox. The manifest edit was made to be correct (second intent-filter added alongside the untouched MAIN/LAUNCHER filter and all permissions), and this APK build plus permission assertion is relied upon via the CI android job. flutter analyze and flutter test do not require the Android SDK and were run and pass locally. Did NOT push or open a PR (orchestrator handles publishing).
